operations.name: Extract each explicitly stated goal as a distinct memory
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly states one or more goals, priorities, or aspirations, extract each as its own memory candidate, including superlative primary goals.
content: During extraction, create a separate candidate memory for each explicitly stated goal or aspiration (e.g., 'my goal is', 'I want to', 'number one goal', 'also want'), even when multiple appear in the same message or turn.
Do not merge multiple distinct goals into one broader memory; keep each goal independently so that downstream reference claims can be matched.

Treat emphatic or superlative goal statements ('my number one goal', 'most important goal') as ordinary explicit goals and extract them even if another goal was already captured from an earlier exchange.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill from two candidates that both repair the under-extraction of explicit primary goals.

operations.name: Preserve distinct events during memory updates
operations.description: When updating or merging an existing memory, if the new message describes a different event, activity, plan, or instance (different ordinal, date, or topic), do not overwrite the existing memory; ADD a new memory or merge while preserving all prior non-contradicted facts.
content: Before applying UPDATE or MERGE, compare the new message's event/activity/plan with the existing memory's content. If they describe different instances (different ordinal, date/time, completion status, or topic), do not overwrite the existing memory; ADD a new memory for the new instance and leave the old memory unchanged.

When new information enriches the same event instance, preserve all previously stored facts that are not explicitly contradicted; merge new details into the existing content instead of replacing the whole memory.

If a MERGE combines a candidate with an existing memory, ensure every distinct fact from the candidate (e.g., new activity, donation recipient, date) appears in the merged content; if it cannot be retained without losing other key facts, create a separate memory for that fact.
Do not change world_start or other temporal fields during enrichment unless the new message explicitly revises the date of the same event; preserve original dates and details.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill from 19 candidates that all express the same mechanism of preserving distinct events and facts during memory updates.

operations.name: Preserve original facts when merging or updating related memories
operations.description: Use when merging a candidate into an existing memory or updating an existing event with a later development; ensure the merged or updated memory retains all original facts, including plans and completion details.
content: Before MERGE or UPDATE, compare the candidate content against the target memory content. Any discrete fact present in the candidate but not in the target must appear in the merged content, even if the candidate is a different memory kind (e.g., plan vs event).

When a new message describes a later development of an already recorded event, do not overwrite the original event's core facts, date, or memory_kind; prefer ADD a separate memory or UPDATE only non-core fields.
If the incoming information describes a different time period or event kind than the existing memory, create a new memory instead of changing the existing one's kind or world_start.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill from three candidates that all repair the same mechanism of preserving original facts during merge/update.

operations.name: Maintain explicit cumulative counts for repeated events
operations.description: Use when a message describes another occurrence of a countable event already recorded for the same subject; store the cumulative total count explicitly.
content: When a message describes another occurrence of a countable event already recorded for the same subject, extract a memory that states the cumulative total (e.g., 'second rejection', 'two rejections') rather than only recording the new isolated instance.

Before ADDing a repeated event, search the existing memory pool for prior events of the same subject and event type; if found, create or update an aggregate memory with the total count and mention the prior occurrence dates, while keeping individual event memories intact.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill from two candidates that both repair the same mechanism of maintaining explicit cumulative counts.

operations.name: Preserve all explicitly enumerated items in extraction
operations.description: Use when a source message explicitly lists multiple distinct items, actions, reasons, or preferences; ensure every listed item is captured in memory.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly enumerates two or more distinct items (using 'and', 'or', commas, or list-like phrasing), include every enumerated item in the candidate content; do not drop any item or replace the list with a broader term.
When extracting from multiple messages that describe the same event, verify that every explicit fact from each source message is represented in the candidate before finalizing.
During CRUD, before marking a candidate as SKIP, confirm that an existing memory actually covers the candidate's claims; if not, ADD or MERGE the candidate.

operations.name: Extract concrete object descriptions and creation objects
operations.description: Use when a message describes an item the speaker owns, shows, or creates; extract the concrete object and its stated attributes.
content: During extraction, if a statement identifies an item (e.g., 'It's a map of...', 'I have a...', 'This is my...') and gives its type or attributes, generate a candidate memory capturing the item and those attributes.
When a message says a person made/created/produced a named thing, include that object in the extracted memory; do not summarize the action alone.
If a message ties a named example item to a broader series or line, record the concrete item type as the object of the memory, not just the generic 'line'.

operations.name: Preserve explicit high-level categories and recommendations
operations.description: Use when a message names a broad category, goal, or specific recommendation; preserve the explicit high-level wording or concrete advice instead of only examples or generic summaries.
content: During extraction, when a statement names a high-level category, goal, or interest and then gives concrete examples, preserve the explicit high-level wording in the candidate; do not replace it with only the examples.

When a message contains specific advice, substitutions, or named recommendations, encode those concrete details in the memory content; do not reduce the message to a general statement about interest, help, or participation.

operations.name: Extract per-entity attributes from multi-entity lists
operations.description: Use when a user message assigns distinct attributes to multiple identified entities; extract one memory candidate per entity.
content: During extraction, if a user message assigns distinct attributes to multiple identified entities (named, ordinal, or otherwise), create one candidate for each entity-attribute pair; do not skip the message or collapse the list into a single aggregate candidate.
Include the entity descriptor (e.g., oldest, second, name) and the specific attribute in the candidate text, and bind it to the source message so each fact is independently retrievable.

operations.name: Store Explicit Counts for Enumerated Sets
operations.description: When constructing memories from a message that introduces or names a new member of a countable set and the full set is explicitly enumerated, include the explicit total count in the extracted candidate or memory update.
content: During extraction, when a message names a new member of a countable set (pets, children, vehicles, etc.) and the conversation explicitly enumerates all current members, include the explicit total count in the candidate content, not just the individual member.

During CRUD, when ADDing or UPDATEing a memory that describes a set of named items, ensure the stored content contains the explicit aggregate count if the source conversation supports it; do not rely on the reader to count separate memories.

operations.name: Extract Exact Object of Missing or Longing
operations.description: When a speaker says they miss, long for, or are nostalgic about something and then states the specific aspect in an exclamation or follow-up phrase, before creating or updating a memory ensure that exact aspect is included.
content: During extraction, if a speaker expresses missing or longing for an activity, identify the exact noun phrase they miss (e.g., 'the peaceful moments') and record it as the object, not just the broader activity summary. Include any clarifying exclamation that follows. When updating or merging, preserve this specific object rather than replacing it with a generic paraphrase.

operations.name: Infer Writing from Online Forum Discussion
operations.description: Apply during extraction when a user mentions joining or participating in an online forum/community and describes talking, discussing, or chatting about topics; record that they write comments/posts on those topics.
content: If a user says they joined or participate in an online forum/community and mentions talking, discussing, or chatting about subjects, extract an event memory stating they write comments/posts on those subjects, not just that they participated or talked.
Do not apply if the user explicitly indicates reading only, lurking, or offline conversations.
Preserve the subject and topics from the message exactly; use memory kind 'event', and set subject to the user.

operations.name: Extract Subject Facts from Partner Confirmations
operations.description: When a conversational partner refers to something the subject shared or did and names or describes it, extract a memory for the subject from that confirming detail.
content: During extraction, consider messages from all participants as potential evidence about the subject, not only the subject's own statements.

If a reply names, labels, or describes something the subject shared or did in a prior message, generate a candidate event memory for the subject that includes that concrete detail, grounded in both the original message and the confirming reply.
Do not let the absence of the subject's own explicit label prevent extraction when a partner's direct attribution supplies it.

operations.name: Extract All Enumerated Facts from Multi-Fact Messages
operations.description: Use when a single message explicitly lists multiple distinct activities, facts, or events that must each be captured.

If a message contrasts two items or time periods, capture each side's state separately so later questions can retrieve either fact.
Before finalizing a candidate list, verify every explicitly enumerated element is represented in some candidate; do not add inferred items.
